Prevention: Use clean seeds/resistant varieties/less susceptible varieties (e.g.
Note: local varieties are highly susceptible (e. g.
Plant early to avoid heavy infestation (September)
Intercrop cowpea with maize or sorghum
Remove host plants (weeds) at 3 and 6 weeks after planting
Plough and harrow to destroy/ kill larvae or pupae
Monitoring: Scout 30 days after planting to look for signs and symptoms of thrips infestations:
White or silvery patches and streaks on leaves, fruits and pods; Open flower buds to look for larvae and adult thrips
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Uproot and burn infested plants away from the crop field
Use botanicals of plant origin (e.g. neem, papaya and siam weed) using the following process:
Get 1 gallon of clean water and divide it equally into 4 different containers
Grind 200 g [one handful] of leaf extracts and add water to prepare solution
Divide a laundry soap bar [e.g. 72% soap] into four equal parts and add one part of the soap to 2 litres of boiling water in a large container.
Stir to melt the soap into the water.
Add half a tomato cupful [35 ml] of kerosene to the soap mixture
Add each of the four leaves mixture to the soap and kerosene mix
Pour solution on a cloth to filter/remove debris.
The final mixture should not have any debris in it to avoid clogging the sprayer nozzle.
Spray the prepared solution using knapsack sprayer or plastic bottle with perforated cover/lid
Spray once per week in the morning or in the evening.
Apply at most two times per planting season.
Restrictions: II (Moderately hazardous); Re- entry period: 2 weeks; Pre- harvest interval: 2 weeks; Early in the morning or late in the evening; Maximum number of application:
